comparator.academicYear: 2026–2027 adopted OER; ordinary current entrant requirements
comparator.sourceNotes: Fresh 1 November 2026 inspection of adopted 2026–2027 OER, Articles7–11, final outcomes and Marine Technology programme appendix: 26 unique components, 60+60+60=180 EC; 30-EC university-approved thematic or examination-board-approved individual minor remains open. Four mathematics parents include their uncredited subparts. Integration and Skills1/2/3 total20EC; separate Ship Design6EC is not a duplicate. Current MT1466-26 applies. Final project14EC controls over older webpage12EC. Entry requires all first-year courses and at least54 second-year EC; results through Q2 second exam period govern the ordinary semester2 start in week3. Completing both years before the minor/final project provides a valid ordinary pathway. Practical participation obligations remain applicable. Dutch full-time programme; English course labels are translations. No formal track instantiated.

programmes.label: Bachelor Marine Technology at Delft University of Technology

exception.reason: The strongest tested UCR response combines mathematical modelling, signals and feedback, robotics, materials, energy assessment, product design, marine ecology and delta infrastructure. It is mechanically feasible and provides genuine technical and environmental study. Its recurring objects are computational systems, energy options, consumer products and coastal ecosystems, however; it does not sustain the analysis and integrated design of vessels and floating structures that defines Marine Technology. Broad sustainability or computing additions cannot supply that organising substance across a complete programme. This is a programme-level academic judgment, not a requirement for identical courses, a professional licence or the degree title.
exception.curriculumContext: The verified full-time Dutch programme contains 26 components totalling180EC, including open approved minor30EC and final project14EC. All first-year courses and at least54 second-year EC are required before the project; the ordinary pathway completes both years first. No older12EC project, parent/child duplicate or invented minor content is used.
exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Current workbook evidence gives Linear Systems real convolution, Fourier/Laplace/Z transforms, sampling, filtering and feedback; no unsupported state-space or transfer-function claim is retained. Sustainability Essentials I/II include actual thermodynamic/mechanical principles, biopolymer strength, wave behaviour and stress/strain. Energy & Sustainability is offered in 2028h2 and contributes real conversion technologies, grids/storage, quantitative appraisal and practical work; the former unavailable-course claim is removed. Robotics provides kinematics, arm/gripper programming and motion planning. Consumer Product Design supplies mechanisms, customer requirements, specifications, concepts, prototypes and production planning. Marine Biology supplies oceanographic and ecological systems; Building with Nature and Living with Water supply ports, coastal infrastructure and delta interventions. Advanced Calculus and Renewable System Design receive full consideration from their descriptions. These strengthen the candidate materially, but do not provide sustained vessel hydromechanics, hull/structural-load analysis, stability, propulsion integration and floating-system design. No hypothetical maritime topic is guaranteed for the partner-dependent Research in a Sustainable Delta project. The archived feasible24-course attempt distinguishes mechanical feasibility from academic acceptance.

candidateAssessment.concept: Vessel design, hydromechanics, propulsion and stability
candidateAssessment.assessment: The strengthened feasible candidate supplies real mathematical, computational, robotic, materials and product-design work. Yet it cannot centre a complete programme on vessel behaviour and integrated floating-system design: the missing object-specific mechanical/structural/propulsion progression is central academic content, not simply a missing professional title. Rejected academically after the mechanical challenge.

Building with Nature, Living with Water, Marine Biology and GIS directly support coastal/port environments and infrastructure evaluation. They organise study around environmental intervention, ecology and adaptation, without sufficient offshore floating structures, subsea technology or dredging-system design to implement this candidate as a full target-related programme.

candidateAssessment.concept: Maritime transport, ship production and vessel operations
candidateAssessment.assessment: Algorithms, optimisation, economics and product production planning offer real methods. Their actual settings do not sustain maritime transport demand, vessel operations and shipyard production as an organising programme. Generic business courses cannot be used merely to reach24; no later alternative is accepted after the closest response fails.

candidateAssessment.concept: Sustainable shipping and vessel performance innovation
candidateAssessment.assessment: Real marine ecology, life-cycle analysis, energy conversion/storage, renewable-system design and coastal research strengthen this direction. Their sustained focus remains general energy/environmental appraisal rather than vessel performance and maritime-system innovation; a partner-dependent project cannot guarantee the missing domain study. Retain rejection without claiming that energy or design is absent.

audience.programmeDescription: Delft’s Marine Technology bachelor studies the physical behaviour and design of ships and other floating structures. Mathematics, mechanics, hydromechanics, propulsion and structures are integrated through design projects, followed by a minor and a final research or design project.
audience.comparisonExplanation: UCR offers related mathematical modelling, robotics, energy, product-design and marine-environment study. These do not combine into a sustained programme centred on the analysis and integrated design of vessels and floating structures. A full UCR comparison is therefore not offered.

curriculum.limitation: The 30-EC minor remains open subject to approval. The 14-EC final project requires all first-year courses and at least 54 EC from year two.
